problem: Temporal Knowledge Graph QA: prior TKG-embedding and GNN methods fail to understand complex semantic information in time constraints, and LLMs suffer temporal hallucination.
method: TimeR4: a Time-aware Retrieve-Rewrite-Retrieve-Rerank framework. A retrieve-rewrite module rewrites the question using TKG background knowledge to obtain explicit time constraints; a retriever is fine-tuned with a contrastive time-aware learning objective to retrieve semantically and temporally relevant facts; retrieved facts are reranked according to the temporal constraints.
key_assumptions: Temporal knowledge is represented as timestamped graph facts
Time constraints can be made explicit by rewriting the question against the KG
A contrastively fine-tuned retriever is needed to capture temporal relevance
main_contribution: A time-aware retrieve-rewrite-rerank framework for TKGQA with relative gains of 47.8% and 22.5% on two datasets.
datasets: Two temporal knowledge graph QA datasets (names not stated in the abstract)
benchmarks: Two TKGQA datasets (not named in the abstract)
baselines: Prior TKG-embedding and GNN-based TKGQA methods (not individually named in the abstract)
metrics: Not stated in abstract (relative improvement percentages reported)
results: Relative gains of 47.8% and 22.5% on two datasets.
limitations: Operates over structured temporal knowledge graphs rather than versioned prose documents
Requires contrastive retriever fine-tuning, contradicting a training-free retrieval-agnostic wrapper
Dataset names, metrics and limitations are not available from the abstract; full text is not open access

relation_to_idea.conceptual_difference: TimeR4 handles explicit temporal constraints over knowledge-graph facts with a learned time-aware retriever; the proposed idea is a training-free, retrieval-agnostic score adjustment over textual document versions distinguished by version timestamps.
relation_to_idea.basis: Both introduce a temporal dimension into retrieval and reranking, but this works on structured timestamped facts and fine-tunes the retriever. Basis is the abstract only.
